lesson.title: Joint control in practice: website plug-ins
lesson.summary: Use Fashion ID to see how far joint control reaches when a website embeds a third-party plug-in.

prerequisites.reason: The case refines when and how far joint control applies.
The case requires each joint controller to have a legitimate interest.

blocks: Joint controllers decide purposes and means together (Article 26). But **how far** does joint control reach? *Fashion ID* (Case C-40/17, 29 July 2019) gives a practical answer.

The case was decided under the GDPR's predecessor, Directive 95/46/EC. That directive defined a controller with the same words as Article 4(7): one who "determines the purposes and means of the processing".

sources.title: CJEU C-40/17 Fashion ID, operative part, points 2-3, and paragraph 84

blocks: **The facts in outline**: a website embedded a social plug-in. When a visitor opened the page, the plug-in made the visitor's browser request content from the plug-in provider, transmitting the visitor's personal data to that provider.

sources.title: CJEU C-40/17 Fashion ID, operative part, points 2-3, and paragraph 84

blocks: **Point 2**: the website operator **can be a controller**. In its reasoning (paragraph 84), the Court treats it as a controller **jointly with the provider**.

But that responsibility is **limited** to the operations for which it actually determines the purposes and means: the **collection and disclosure by transmission** of the data. It does not cover what the provider does with the data afterwards.

sources.title: CJEU C-40/17 Fashion ID, operative part, points 2-3, and paragraph 84

blocks: **Point 3**: for those operations to be justified, the operator **and** the provider must **each** pursue a legitimate interest, under the old directive's Article 7(f).
Under the GDPR, the legitimate-interests basis is Article 6(1)(f).

sources.title: CJEU C-40/17 Fashion ID, operative part, points 2-3, and paragraph 84

blocks: If Sunfield embeds a social-media button that sends visitor data to the platform as soon as the page loads, Sunfield may be a joint controller for that collection and transmission.
It would then need an Article 26 arrangement, transparency for visitors and a legal basis. It would not become responsible for the platform's later processing.

blocks.text: These Sunfield examples are **illustrations**. A real assessment depends on all the facts.

sources.title: CJEU C-40/17 Fashion ID, operative part, points 2-3, and paragraph 84

questions.prompt: A website embeds a plug-in that sends visitors' data to the plug-in provider. Can the website operator be a controller?

options.blocks: Yes, jointly, for the collection and transmission
No, only the plug-in provider is a controller
options.reason: The Court held the operator can be a controller.

options.blocks: Yes, for everything the provider does later
options.reason: Responsibility is limited to the operations it co-determines.

variants.prompt: Under Fashion ID, can the website operator be a controller for the plug-in's data flow?

options.blocks: No, only the plug-in provider is a controller
options.reason: The Court held the operator can be a controller.

options.blocks: Yes, for everything the provider does later
options.reason: Responsibility is limited to the operations it co-determines.

options.blocks: Yes, jointly, for the collection and transmission

questions.prompt: How far does the website operator's responsibility reach?

options.blocks: All later processing by the provider
None, once visitors accept the site's terms
options.reason: Terms do not change the controller analysis.

options.blocks: Collection and disclosure by transmission only
options.reason: Point 2 limits it to these operations.

variants.prompt: Which operations does the operator jointly control according to Fashion ID?

options.blocks: None, once visitors accept the site's terms
options.reason: Terms do not change the controller analysis.

options.blocks: Collection and disclosure by transmission only
options.reason: Point 2 limits it to these operations.

options.blocks: All later processing by the provider

questions.prompt: According to Fashion ID, whose legitimate interest must exist for these operations?

options.blocks: Neither's, because they are joint controllers
options.reason: Joint control does not remove the need for a legal basis.

options.blocks: Both the operator's and the provider's
options.reason: Point 3: each must pursue a legitimate interest.

variants.prompt: In Fashion ID, whose legitimate interests had to exist for the plug-in's data flow?

options.blocks: Both the operator's and the provider's
options.reason: Point 3: each must pursue a legitimate interest.
